title: BRICS 8th Ocean and Polar Science and Technology working group meeting
body_text:
Ministry of Earth Sciences (MoES) organized the 8th Meeting of the BRICS Working Group on Ocean Polar Science and Technology (OPST) at Goa, hosted by the National Centre for Polar and Ocean Research (NCPOR) from 12–14 August 2026 during India’s BRICS Presidency. Since the establishment of the BRICS OPST Working Group, the activities are conducted by MoES in coordination with the Department Science and Technology (DST), Govt. of India under the framework of Science, Technology and Innovation (STI) cooperation activities among BRICS member countries. The meeting brought together senior officials, scientists, experts, and representatives from Brazil, China, Egypt, India, Indonesia, Russia, South Africa, and the United Arab Emirates to deliberate on areas of mutual interest and further strengthen cooperation in ocean and polar science and technology. The meeting was inaugurated on 12 th August by Dr. Thamban Meloth, Director, NCPOR and Dr. Madhavan Nair Rajeevan, VC Atria University and former Secretary of MoES graced as Chief Guest. The 3 days long event was Chaired by Director, NCPOR, Goa and attended by the delegations from BRICS member countries. The Indian delegation was constituted of officials and scientists from MoES, DST, and headed by Dr. Sandip Kumar Mukhopadhyay, Scientist G & Advisor, MoES.
This working group meeting acted as a platform for deliberations and discussions on scientific cooperation, exchange of knowledge, capacity building and development of collaborative research activities among BRICS member countries in the field of Ocean and Polar research. The deliberations were focused on the issues and opportunities of BRICS countries like challenges of the costal zones with special emphasis on protection of coastal cities; strengthening the Global Ocean Observing System (GOOS) through collaborative contribution for the development of robust and resilient ocean information services; development of joint polar research and inclusive participation in the Antarctic Expedition; enhanced opportunities for capacity building in particular for young researchers. During the meeting the delegations of BRICS countries jointly agreed for collaborative initiative in building up coastal resilience, carrying out joint polar ocean biodiversity study, setting milestones for International Polar Year – 5 and promoting capacity building of young researchers. During BRICS Presidency India will coordinate for finalisation of the ongoing work on the development of roadmap for the Working Group including the action plan for its short-term implementation.
Addressing the concluding session of the 8th Meeting of the BRICS-OPST through virtual mode, Dr. T. Srinivasa Kumar Tummala, Secretary, Ministry of Earth Sciences (MoES), Government of India, expressed his appreciation to the delegates from BRICS member countries for the fruitful deliberations and outcomes of the three-day meeting held in Goa. He noted that the meeting had provided a valuable platform for strengthening scientific cooperation in ocean and polar sciences. The Secretary expressed satisfaction over the consensus reached on key priority areas and encouraged member countries to translate the outcomes of the meeting into concrete collaborative actions, including joint research initiatives, exchange of scientists and students, sharing of research infrastructure, and strengthening institutional linkages. He expressed his confidence that the recommendations and outcomes of the meeting would further strengthen BRICS cooperation in ocean and polar science and technology. The meeting ended reaffirming the commitment of BRICS countries to advancing ocean and polar science and technology through collaborative efforts and strengthened partnerships.

enrichment.summary: The Ministry of Earth Sciences, through NCPOR, hosted the 8th BRICS Working Group on Ocean Polar Science and Technology (OPST) in Goa from 12-14 August 2026 during India's BRICS Presidency. Delegates from Brazil, China, Egypt, India, Indonesia, Russia, South Africa and the UAE discussed coastal resilience, strengthening the Global Ocean Observing System, joint polar research, and capacity building for young researchers. The meeting concluded with agreement on collaborative initiatives including coastal resilience building, joint polar ocean biodiversity studies, and milestones for International Polar Year-5.
enrichment.context: The BRICS OPST Working Group operates under the bloc's Science, Technology and Innovation (STI) cooperation framework, coordinated by India's Ministry of Earth Sciences and Department of Science and Technology. With India holding the BRICS Presidency in 2026, such working groups gain added significance as India seeks to shape the agenda for scientific and technological collaboration among emerging economies, including newer BRICS members like Egypt, Indonesia and the UAE (following the bloc's 2024 expansion). Ocean and polar science cooperation is increasingly important given shared concerns among BRICS nations about coastal vulnerability, climate change impacts, and the need for pooled resources in expensive polar research (such as Antarctic expeditions), which few countries can undertake alone. NCPOR, based in Goa, is India's nodal agency for polar and ocean research and has historically led India's Antarctic and Arctic expeditions, making it a natural host for this technical diplomacy. The reference to 'International Polar Year-5' relates to a periodic international scientific collaboration initiative (previous Polar Years occurred in 1882-83, 1932-33, 1957-58, and 2007-08) coordinated globally to intensify polar research through coordinated observations, and BRICS coordination on this signals an attempt to build a common southern-hemisphere/emerging-economy voice in global polar governance alongside established Arctic Council and Antarctic Treaty System frameworks dominated by developed nations.

prelims_questions.question: The National Centre for Polar and Ocean Research (NCPOR), which hosted the 8th BRICS OPST Working Group meeting, is located in which Indian state?
prelims_questions.explanation: NCPOR, India's nodal agency for polar and ocean research, is based in Goa, as stated in the release.

prelims_questions.question: Which of the following countries was NOT mentioned as a participant in the 8th BRICS OPST Working Group meeting held in Goa in 2026?
prelims_questions.explanation: The release lists Brazil, China, Egypt, India, Indonesia, Russia, South Africa and the UAE as participants; Saudi Arabia is not mentioned despite being a BRICS member, making it the correct 'not mentioned' option in this context.

mains_questions.question: Discuss the significance of multilateral scientific cooperation platforms like the BRICS Ocean and Polar Science and Technology Working Group in addressing shared environmental and climate challenges faced by member nations.
Examine the importance of polar and ocean research for coastal resilience and climate adaptation in the context of India's expanding role in international scientific diplomacy.

study_notes.reason: NCPOR and the BRICS OPST framework provide a testable factual core (nodal agency, member composition, host location), while India's BRICS presidency and the push for a common emerging-economy voice in polar governance offer genuine analytical material on scientific diplomacy.

prelims.point: NCPOR (National Centre for Polar and Ocean Research), based in Goa, is India's nodal agency for polar and ocean research under the Ministry of Earth Sciences, and hosted the 8th BRICS OPST meeting.
prelims.why_important: NCPOR's role and parent ministry are a classic institution-ministry pairing UPSC tests, and its Goa location plus polar/ocean research mandate is distinctive.

prelims.point: BRICS expanded in 2024 to include new members such as Egypt, Indonesia, and the UAE, all of whom participated in this OPST meeting.
prelims.why_important: BRICS composition changes are a recurring current-affairs prelims theme, especially distinguishing original vs newly added members.

prelims.point: The BRICS OPST Working Group functions under the bloc's Science, Technology and Innovation (STI) cooperation framework, jointly coordinated by India's Ministry of Earth Sciences and Department of Science and Technology.
prelims.why_important: Tests knowledge of which ministries jointly coordinate specific BRICS sectoral cooperation mechanisms.

prelims.point: International Polar Year is a periodic global scientific collaboration initiative, with previous editions in 1882-83, 1932-33, 1957-58 and 2007-08; a fifth edition is now being planned.
prelims.why_important: Chronological facts about international scientific collaboration initiatives are a favoured objective-question format.

mains.point: BRICS ocean-polar cooperation reflects an attempt by emerging economies to pool resources for expensive polar research (e.g., Antarctic expeditions) that few individual countries can afford alone.
mains.analytical_use: Useful for questions on why developing/emerging economies pursue multilateral scientific cooperation frameworks and the rationale behind cost-sharing in big science.

mains.point: India's coordination of BRICS OPST during its 2026 presidency signals an effort to shape a common southern-hemisphere/emerging-economy voice in global polar governance, alongside Arctic Council and Antarctic Treaty System structures dominated by developed nations.
mains.theme: India's scientific diplomacy and polar governance
mains.analytical_use: Relevant for questions on India's use of multilateral platforms to advance strategic and scientific interests, or on the geopolitics of polar governance.

mains.point: Coastal resilience and protection of coastal cities emerged as a shared priority among BRICS nations, reflecting common vulnerability to climate change impacts.
mains.analytical_use: Can support answers on climate adaptation cooperation among developing nations or South-South cooperation on environmental challenges.

mains.point: The meeting emphasised capacity building for young researchers as a means of sustaining long-term scientific cooperation among BRICS countries.
mains.theme: Capacity building in international scientific cooperation
mains.analytical_use: Useful as a supporting point in answers on strengthening institutional and human capital dimensions of multilateral cooperation.
